stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy technician's license has been expired for 26 months. The technician submits the renewal form and fees, but the Board has not renewed the license or decided whether to impose additional conditions. The pharmacy wants the technician to begin work under direct pharmacist supervision. Which statement is most accurate?

choices.text: Submitting the form and fees restores the license provisionally while the Board reviews the application.
Direct pharmacist supervision may permit practice during the renewal review despite the expired license.
A lapse exceeding two years automatically requires a specified national technician examination before renewal.
The technician cannot practice until renewal; because the lapse exceeded two years, additional Board conditions may apply.
A lapse exceeding two years permanently bars renewal of the technician license.

explanation.core_reasoning: Practice after expiration is unlicensed practice. A technician seeking renewal after a lapse exceeding two years may be required to satisfy additional conditions determined by the Board. The regulation does not itself prescribe one automatic examination for every such applicant, and filing alone does not restore authority to practice.

choice_analysis.A: An application and payment do not constitute renewal or create provisional practice authority.
choice_analysis.B: Supervision is required for licensed technician practice, but it does not cure the absence of a current license.
choice_analysis.C: The Board may set additional conditions, but the regulation does not automatically name a particular examination for every lapse over two years.
choice_analysis.D: Correct: renewal must occur before practice, and the duration of lapse opens the Board-determined-conditions pathway.
choice_analysis.E: The regulation provides a renewal route rather than a permanent bar.

related_facts: Technician licenses expire on the applicable birthday-based cycle specified by the regulation.
Renewal fees and late charges are distinct from any additional conditions the Board may impose after a long lapse.
explanation.mpje_trap: A discretionary power to impose conditions should not be converted into an automatic named-exam rule, but it also does not create interim practice authority.

reasoning_steps: Classify the lapse as exceeding two years
Apply the no-practice consequence until renewal
Distinguish Board-determined additional conditions from an automatic exam requirement
